articles.Title: ​Eating just before bed? Late-night snacking might be raising your risk of fatty liver disease, study warns​
articles.Description: We’ve all been there: staring at the fridge late at night, grabbing a quick snack before bed or just finishing dinner during a late shift. For a lot of us, it’s routine. But new research is raising red flags about what late-night eating means for more than just your waistline. The analysis drew on three large US health studies involving 199,155 participants followed for a median of 16 years.The study published in Clinical Gastroenterology and Hepatology suggests that meal timing might matter as much as what you eat or how much. Scientists looked at nearly 200,000 adults in the US and found that regular late-night eating is linked with a higher chance of developing fatty liver disease and cirrhosis, which is a serious form of liver scarring. However, researchers are careful to note that they found an association, not definitive proof that late-night snacking causes liver trouble. Still, the numbers are hard to ignore.
